newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CHINA AND U.S. TIPPED AS WORLD CUP CHALLENGERS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CHINA AND U.S. TIPPED AS WORLD CUP CHALLENGERS.

text.p: China and the United States could emerge as serious challengers for the 2007 Rugby World Cup, Cup co-director Vernon Pugh said on Thursday.

Pugh, and World Cup chairman Leo Williams, discussing details of the 1999 World Cup in Wales, both predicted future tournaments would bear a very different look to the past three competitions dominated by the southern hemisphere.
"In eight years time or thereabouts, we'll find countries competing against teams we would never expected at this moment in time," said Pugh.

"I think we'll be surprised by the speed of it. The U.S. for example is a country chockfull of excellent athletes. Now the sport has gone professional, if they can devote their energies towards rugby they can become a major force.
"Likewise, China are shortly to become members of the International Rugby Board. They have all the attributes required to field a successful rugby side. I'd be very surprised if they don't develop."
Qualifying for the 1999 tournament starts this weekend in the unlikely rugby venue of Riga where Latvia host Norway, but details of the format for the finals are still being discussed.
Williams said Rugby World Cup was looking at ways of earning between 50 and 60 million pounds sterling ($78-$94 million) from the next tournament.
"We made about 20 million pounds ($31 million) profit in 1995...we expect to better that total in 1999,"" he said.
